source_scope.feature: PDF byte offsets and file access
source_scope.effective_requirement: PDF cross-reference structures and startxref identify byte offsets in the file. Annex C.4 discusses a traditional cross-reference-table offset limit as implementation guidance. The clauses do not prescribe Unix descriptors, SCM_RIGHTS, seccomp syscalls, a descriptor quota, or whether a host transfers bytes versus a handle.
source_scope.decision: ADR 0812 is an implementation/confinement decision that carries an already-open file handle and the host-measured length. It preserves the byte-addressed input expected by the parser; the OS transport is not itself a PDF conformance requirement.

source_scope.effective_requirement: Signature validation interprets the declared ByteRange against document bytes. This review records the file-window/error handoff only; it does not re-audit digest, CMS, certificate, timestamp, or signature-policy correctness already assigned to the signature shards.
source_scope.decision: Windowed I/O is compatible with reading the declared byte ranges. Streaming is an implementation choice, not mandated by this PDF transport boundary.

source_scope.consumer: viewer-confined protocol encode/decode → confined-transport host frame → Unix SCM_RIGHTS → worker recvmsg → FileBytes::from_handle → PDF parser
source_scope.assertion_review: Protocol unit test checks wire length, ON_DISK tag, missing-descriptor named refusal, descriptor consumption, memory-byte route, and actual decoded content. Confined integration test opens the committed specification PDF through the sandbox and checks page count, raster dimensions, pixel-for-pixel equality with the memory route, and nonblank ink. Separate kernel probes check pread is allowed and metadata/stat is denied. FileBytes tests check stated lengths shorter/equal/longer than the physical file and prefix descriptor reuse.
source_scope.verdict: The critical descriptor route has both protocol and real host→worker consumer evidence. Existing protocol fixture opens the same pathname independently for the supplied descriptor, so its local 'same file' assertion is not a same-open-file-description identity probe; the integration route does pass FileBytes' actual borrowed descriptor. No source requirement mandates a separate identity regression.

source_scope.implementation: worker read_frame treats UnexpectedEof while filling the fixed frame header as end-of-input; truncation while filling the advertised payload propagates as an I/O error. NoDescriptor and Uncarried are explicit protocol errors; worker drops unclaimed/excess descriptors after decode and refuses malformed command payloads by name. Host maps worker-output EOF to worker-death handling.
source_scope.verdict: This is transport lifecycle/error policy. It is not a PDF-level rule. A partial frame header currently ends the worker as if clean EOF, while a partial payload takes an error path; no user-visible PDF misclassification was identified in the reviewed host API.
